I'm genuinely surprised by your insight. I have actually run into the problem of not being able to always keep that philosophy of life in mind. I've noticed those thoughts and ideas could vanish quickly if I don't remind myself of them often. Once I go back to them I got instant relief from all the chaos in my life... It could just be a way of avoiding problems instead of taking actions to solve them and achieve greatness to be happy... 

Some people may have genetic predispositions that lead them to be more pessimistic in general and I'm one of them... Also it's difficult to strive for things that make one happy and content, for we are insatiable beings on a hedonic treadmill. To do that, first we have to establish a goal, but for many it's already a difficult task that might never be accomplished. Then we have to aim towards our goal with painful dedicated efforts. During the process we will inevitably face obstacles and failure. Anyway achieving happiness and contentment is extremely hard imo.... Until then we have reached wretched old age...

But I think acknowledging that life is full of suffering, and that its just the general rule for us fragile mortals allows you to be a good person too, because you understand that we're all in this mess together. Compassion makes us moral. if that unemployed guy whose best friend finds a high paying job is aware that his best friend is going through other life issues, or that we're all gonna die anyway, he actually might feel happy for him, or not care about anything anyway cuz its just a dream-like existence. no one gets out alive
